name: Daisetsuzan: Asahidake to Kurodake (大雪山 旭岳-黒岳)
why: Across the roof of Hokkaido in a day: from the steaming top of its highest volcano round the rim of a 2 km caldera, with a ropeway at each end.
book: No permit. Bus from Asahikawa to the Asahidake ropeway (about 4 a day) and up to Sugatami. At the end, the Kurodake chairlift and ropeway go down to Sounkyo onsen; check the last run. You can split the walk with a night at the Kurodake Ishimuro hut.
water: Carry 2 litres: nothing to buy between the ropeways. Stream water may carry Echinococcus: boil or filter it.
dangers: Weather turns fast on the open plateau: fog, wind and cold rain even in July. Shell, warm layer and gloves.
Brown bears live in the park: wear a bell and keep food packed.
Snow patches stay all summer; the descent from Asahidake is loose volcanic scree.
Volcanic vents steam beside the trail on Asahidake: do not leave the path.
turnaround: In fog or high wind on Asahidake summit, go back down to Sugatami: the plateau beyond has no shelter until Kurodake Ishimuro.

points.name: Sugatami ropeway station
points.note: Top of the Asahidake ropeway, about 1,600 m. A short nature trail leads east to the ponds.

points.name: Sugatami pond
points.note: The pond that mirrors Asahidake and its steam vents. From here the path climbs 690 m straight up the scree.

points.name: Asahidake summit
points.note: 2,291 m, the highest point of Hokkaido. Down the steep east side past the Ura-Asahi camp, then along the plateau by Mamiyadake.

points.name: Ohachidaira caldera viewpoint
points.note: On the rim of the Ohachidaira caldera, about 2 km across. Snow and alpine flowers inside it in July and August.

points.name: Kurodake summit
points.note: 1,984 m, after the Kurodake Ishimuro hut and camp. The view runs back over the whole plateau.

points.name: Kurodake 7th station lift
points.note: About an hour of steep steps below the summit: the chairlift, then the ropeway, down to Sounkyo onsen.
